reason: E1 supports that Mo-containing HEAs retain high-temperature strength better than others, but does not directly show Mo addition to TiVNbTa improves strength or that Mo acts as a dislocation pinning/diffusion retardant in this specific system. E2 only mentions early Mo-containing HEAs' high-temperature strength without addressing the proposed mechanism or the TiVNbTa system. The baseline properties and structural prediction lack direct cited support.
premises: Mo-containing refractory HEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) show lower reduction in yield strength at elevated temperatures compared to other HEAs.
Mo atoms can act as effective dislocation pinning sites and retard atomic diffusion at high temperatures.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC HEA with yield strength ~330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding Mo to TiVNbTa will retain a single-phase BCC structure with enhanced lattice distortion.
